author: MarioNawfal
text:
🇺🇸🇨🇳 David Woo thinks Washington is fighting China on two fronts without quite admitting it.

The first is Iran.

Woo describes the Iran war as the first modern U.S.-China proxy war, arguing that Chinese technology has helped Tehran absorb enormous American pressure while exposing the limits of U.S. military power.

But the second front may matter far more.

And that's AI.

“The biggest shock of 2026 is how quickly China caught up in the AI race.”

Despite U.S. restrictions on advanced chips and semiconductor equipment, Woo argues Chinese models have closed much of the performance gap while operating far more cheaply. China is simultaneously scaling robotics, EVs and industrial automation.

That leaves Washington with an ugly problem.

Woo believes Trump’s biggest strategic decision may be whether to ban Chinese AI models outright. But he warns that Beijing could answer by restricting rare earths, shattering the fragile U.S.-China economic truce and hitting markets.

And simply blocking China may no longer be enough.

Every restriction gives Beijing another problem to engineer around.

Woo’s final point is even harder to ignore:

American workers are no longer competing with cheap Chinese workers.

They’re competing with cheap Chinese robots now.
